title: Texas conveyances: in writing, and recorded to bind later buyers and creditors
rule: A conveyance of a freehold, an estate of inheritance or an estate for more than one year in land must be in writing, signed and delivered by the grantor or an agent authorized in writing. Unless acknowledged, sworn to or proved and filed for record, a conveyance or deed of trust is void against creditors and later purchasers for value without notice, though it binds the parties and later purchasers with notice. Recording in the proper county gives everyone notice.
changeWatch: Amendments to Property Code chapters 5, 12 or 13. Section 12.001, which sets what an instrument needs to be recorded, was amended effective December 4, 2025 to require photo identification from anyone presenting an instrument in person.
